questionBank.q: Which of the following best explains why a company would choose to revalue its non-current assets periodically rather than relying solely on historical cost?
opts: A. To ensure the balance sheet reflects the assets' true current economic worth, supporting decisions like sales or restructuring
B. Because revaluation is the only method permitted for reporting non-current assets under any accounting framework
C. Because periodic revaluation eliminates the need to ever calculate depreciation in the future
D. Because historical cost is always a more accurate reflection of an asset's worth than fair value
questionBank.exp: Periodic revaluation helps ensure the balance sheet reflects an asset's true current economic worth, which can be particularly useful when a company is considering asset sales, mergers, or financial restructuring.

questionBank.q: Why is the distinction between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure important for accurate financial reporting?
opts: A. Because misclassifying one as the other can distort both the balance sheet and the income statement for the period
B. Because capital expenditure and revenue expenditure always produce identical effects on the financial statements
C. Because the distinction only matters for businesses operating exclusively in the banking sector
D. Because revenue expenditure is never permitted to appear on a company's income statement
questionBank.exp: Misclassifying capital expenditure as revenue expenditure (or vice versa) distorts both the balance sheet, by misstating asset values, and the income statement, by misstating expenses for the period.

questionBank.q: Which of the following best explains why the disposal of a non-current asset can result in either a profit or a loss for the business?
opts: A. Because the outcome depends on whether the sale proceeds exceed or fall short of the asset's carrying value at disposal
B. Because disposal of a non-current asset always results in a loss regardless of the sale proceeds received
C. Because disposal of a non-current asset always results in a profit regardless of the sale proceeds received
D. Because the original acquisition cost is irrelevant to determining the outcome of a disposal transaction
questionBank.exp: Whether a disposal results in a profit or loss depends on the relationship between the sale proceeds received and the asset's carrying value (book value) at the time of disposal.

questionBank.q: Why does the manual emphasize that the specific classification and treatment of non-current assets may vary based on the accounting standards applied?
opts: A. Because differing frameworks, such as GAAP and IFRS, may prescribe different rules for recognition and measurement
B. Because non-current asset classification is identical under every accounting framework worldwide
C. Because accounting standards have no influence whatsoever on how non-current assets are reported
D. Because only IFRS permits the classification of any asset as non-current in nature
questionBank.exp: Different accounting frameworks, such as GAAP and IFRS, may prescribe different specific rules for the recognition, measurement, and classification of non-current assets, requiring companies to follow the applicable standard consistently.

questionBank.q: Which of the following best explains why proper depreciation accounting supports more informed decisions about asset replacement?
opts: A. Because tracking an asset's declining book value over time helps management anticipate when it may no longer be cost-effective to maintain
B. Because depreciation accounting has no bearing whatsoever on decisions related to replacing an asset
C. Because assets are automatically replaced once their depreciation calculation reaches zero
D. Because depreciation accounting only affects tax reporting, not internal management decisions
questionBank.exp: By tracking an asset's declining book value over its useful life, depreciation accounting helps management anticipate when an asset may no longer be cost-effective to maintain and should be considered for replacement.
